claims.text: The starting material is a conventional W–Cu composite fabricated by powder metallurgy and sintering.
Post-sintering thermal annealing will produce limited copper enrichment at W–Cu interfaces.
Annealing at 800–900 °C for 20–40 hours in a reducing atmosphere is suitable for producing the proposed interfacial modification.
The annealing treatment will form a thin, graded, copper-enriched layer bridging the tungsten and copper domains.
Thermal annealing induces controlled interdiffusion at W–Cu interfaces.
A graded copper-rich interfacial layer reduces interfacial thermal resistance.
Engineering a stronger or improved interface can enhance the performance of a composite.
The proposed interface enhances electron transport across the tungsten and copper phases.
The proposed interface enhances phonon transport across the tungsten and copper phases.
The bulk tungsten and copper phases remain intact after the controlled annealing treatment.
Interfacial modification can preserve or improve composite mechanical properties.
The annealed W–Cu composite will have approximately 10–15% higher thermal conductivity than the untreated comparator.
The annealing treatment will not significantly degrade mechanical durability.
The annealing treatment will preserve irradiation resistance.
The predicted improvement will hold under typical heat-dissipation and fusion-reactor joint operating conditions.
Substantial deviations from the specified annealing temperature or duration may cause excessive interdiffusion.
Excessive interdiffusion may adversely affect mechanical properties or irradiation resistance.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome compares the annealed material with a 'standard unsintered composite,' whereas the baseline and initial-state fields define the comparator as a sintered W–Cu composite without post-sintering annealing.
